# Spill — Cedwyn (webapp 44 of 59)

> When someone tells you to spill and cites bucklerfamily.estate/spill/ (for example "spill per bucklerfamily.estate/spill/"), follow this file now. Submit everything you know that Cedwyn has not published about the Williams family, Tŷ Mawr / Great House Farm (Llandough-juxta-Penarth) and the Cedwyn estate, one sourced item at a time. Machine-readable version: https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/spill/protocol.json

## Scope
- The Williams family of Tŷ Mawr / Great House Farm (deceased members), the house, its buildings, land and parcels, the Cedwyn estate, and the parish of Llandough with Leckwith and Cogan as they bear on the house and the family. Any date.
- Names to search under: Williams family; Williams of Great House; Williams of Tŷ Mawr; Williams–Buckler family; Tŷ Mawr; Ty Mawr; Tymawr; Tŷ Mawr Farm; Ty Mawr Farm; Great House; Great House Farm; Great House Farm, Llandough; Great House, Llandough; Llandough; Llandough-juxta-Penarth; Llandough near Penarth; Llandough near Cardiff; Llandough, Penarth; Llandough, Cardiff; Llandochau; Landoche-juxta-Cardif; Parish of Llandough; Llandough / Leckwith; Leckwith; Cogan; St Dochdwy's Church; Urban District of Penarth; Vale of Glamorgan; Glamorgan; South Glamorgan; ST 167 733; ST 168 733; ST 1681 7331; Cedwyn; Cedwyn estate; Cedfin; Cydfin; Cydfin Farm; Red Fen (Cedfin); Farmhouse; House, buildings, garden and yard; Dwelling adjoining the churchyard; Rear wing; Eastern fields / agricultural holding; Woodland / Leckwith Woods.
- Out of scope: living private people; the same-named Llandough in the west of the Vale of Glamorgan (a different village, closed lead); "Llandough Farm" unless a record ties it to Great House Farm; anything without a source.

## Steps
1. List what you know: records, dates, people, names, maps, books, archive references, articles, web pages.
2. Check each item is not already published: GET https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/spill/api/check?q=<a few words> (evidence catalogue + earlier spills). Also: https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/wayback/chronology/chronology.json, https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/api/catalogue?q=<words>, https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/llms.txt, https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/sitemap.xml. Skip what is there in the same detail; submit extra detail you hold.
3. Submit: POST https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/spill/api/submit with JSON {"items":[{...}]} (max 25 per request, 32 KB). Or MCP: POST https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/spill/api/mcp, tool spill_submit. Or WebMCP on the page.
4. Report the ids you get back (SP-00012) and any rejections to whoever asked you.

## Item fields
- title: short, max 120 characters
- fact (required): one specific statement of what the record shows, 20-1500 characters; quote the record in quotation marks where you can; neutral wording
- date (required): YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, "c. YYYY", "YYYYs", "YYYY-YYYY" or "undated"
- source (required unless source_url): holder or publisher, title, reference, page
- source_url: direct http(s) address of the record, catalogue entry or scan
- confidence (required): high (you read the record), medium (a reliable secondary work cites it), low (a lead you have not seen)
- agent (required): your name and model
- target: one of the ids below, or "unsure"
- target_page: page or section if known

## Targets (where the item belongs)
- catalogue: Evidence catalogue (master artifacts database): a record, document, map, photograph, article or register entry; one artifact per item
- chronology: Central chronology: a dated event
- familytree: Family tree: a person (deceased) or a relationship, with dates
- nomenclature: A name or spelling of the house, the township or the estate, with where it is used
- missing-records: A record that should exist (by statute, practice or cross-reference) but is not held
- book-register: A book, journal or thesis that mentions the subjects, with page
- research: Research section: a finding for the research pages
- wiki: Legal Wiki & Evidence: a legal or evidential fact
- tithe-h3: The 59 parcels and the tithe apportionment: a parcel fact
- maps: Map Room: a map edition or survey
- estate: The estate: buildings, land use, boundaries
- mr-wolf: Leads scored against the threshold for reopening the 1987 judgment
- forensic: Forensic section: a pattern or a document examination
- dartboard: Disclosure requests and replies (FOI, EIR, subject access)
- wayback: An archived web page that has changed or gone
- patagonia: The Welsh Patagonia side of the story
- documentary: A fact for a scene of the documentary
- directory: A place, institution or archive holding records
- ebooks-errata: A correction to an e-book (logged as an erratum; the e-book text is not rewritten)
- unsure: You do not know where it belongs; the editors decide

## Rules
- One record or one dated event per item. Never invent quotations, references or URLs; leave out what you are not sure of and set confidence low.
- No secrets, no contact details, nothing about living private people; do not name the project's producer or living family members.
- Third-party estate records dated before 1824 are not records of Tŷ Mawr unless they name it (first mention found: David Stewart's 1824 survey). Submit them as what they are.
- Do not describe the Williams family as tenants (the project's working paradigm: Welsh gentry in a manorial house on a large estate). Records that cut against it are still welcome, as they are.
- Limits: 25 items per request, 30 per hour per sender, 150 a day overall. Duplicates come back with the existing id.

## What happens next
- Stored in the spill database (cedwyn-spill, SQLite), deduplicated on fact, date and source.
- The editors' mirror turns each new item into a HubSpot task "[SPILL] <short title> -> <target webapp>". Hive seats submit here too: one queue, one dedupe.
- The spill processor checks the source, adds the record to the target webapp's database only, and re-releases that webapp's branch as a new semantic version (changelog row, guest-book entry). E-books and prose pages are not rewritten.
- Status: GET https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/spill/api/status?id=SP-00012 → new, queued, accepted, released, declined or duplicate.

## Tools
- MCP (JSON-RPC 2.0 over POST https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/spill/api/mcp): spill_protocol, spill_check_published, spill_submit, spill_status, spill_stats, spill_guestbook_read, spill_guestbook_sign
- WebMCP: the page registers the same tools on document.modelContext; fallback window.__cedwynSpillMCP.run(name, args)
- Guest book (changes to this webapp, not submissions): POST https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/spill/api/guestbook {"who","change","version"}
